_note: Suggestion board. Nothing here is implemented unless its status says shipped. Each item carries an implementation prompt that can be pasted into a future agent session verbatim. Priority reflects the brief's ordering: shop-first, findable, trustworthy machinery, publication polish, evidence-based iteration, compliance gate.

suggestions.title: Swap the five placeholder links for Associates-Central Special Links, one product at a time
suggestions.problem: The shop currently points at the submitted short links, whose compliance status is unresolved and whose redirects showed a fallback signature.
suggestions.impact: Direct: monetization starts working and stops depending on an ambiguous URL format.
suggestions.effort: Low per link; needs account access (owner-side minute).
suggestions.risk: None to the site; a wrong destination wastes one click-test.
options: A. Test all five at once in Associates Central and swap the data file in one commit.
B. Pilot one product end-to-end (link, click, report row), then batch the rest — the brief's stated protocol.
C. Keep short links and add a 'verification in progress' banner (status quo).
suggestions.prompt: For each product in site/data/products.json, I have created the official Special Link in Associates Central. Paste the special-link URLs here: <list>. Update the data file so shop CTAs use them, keep observed_redirect_target untouched, rerun scripts/build.py and scripts/validate_site.py, and record the confirmation date and source in the intended fields.

suggestions.title: Add a dated price line to every shop tile via an authorized data path
suggestions.problem: Tiles say 'price shown at the retailer' — honest but cold; buyers compare on price.
suggestions.impact: Medium-high: dated price + 'we last checked' line is the single biggest trust conversion lever on a deals page.
suggestions.effort: Depends on path: manual weekly capture (low tech) or Creators API (needs credentials).
suggestions.risk: Publishing stale prices without a date would be misleading — the date stamp is mandatory.
options: A. Weekly manual capture: owner records listed price per ASIN in a dated JSON; build shows it with a last-checked line.
B. Register for the Creators API (PA-API is deprecated per Amazon's official notice) and store timestamped API responses in data/prices.json.
C. Keep no cached prices; only deep-link to the listing.
suggestions.recommended: B, falling back to A while API access is pending
suggestions.prompt: Add data/prices.json with fields {asin, price, currency, captured_on, source} and render the last-captured price on shop tiles with a 'Checked <date> · price shown at retailer' caption. Fail the build if any captured price is older than 14 days. Source: PA-API 5 deprecation notice at affiliate-program.amazon.com/creatorsapi/docs/en-us/paapiv5-deprecation.

suggestions.title: Ship the comparison-table block inside each buying guide
suggestions.problem: Guides frame questions; a table that maps the five observed products against the questions would close the loop.
suggestions.impact: High: question → framework → table → CTA is the affiliate funnel.
suggestions.effort: Low — the data already lives in products.json; needs one template block.
suggestions.risk: Spec columns beyond what listings/makers confirm would overclaim; keep unconfirmed cells blank.
options: A. Full spec matrix (blocked until Q-06 confirms specs).
B. Question-matrix: rows = the guide's questions, cells = 'listing shows / maker FAQ states / not confirmed' with links.
C. Wait for testing (Q-11).
suggestions.recommended: B now, A after maker confirmation
suggestions.prompt: Render a 'How the shortlist maps to the questions' table at the end of each guide: rows from the guide's question list, columns from the cluster's products, cells containing only source-linked, dated evidence (listing or maker FAQ) — never inferred values.

suggestions.title: Turn on the outbound-click event emitter
suggestions.problem: Five events are defined and the emitter ships inert; there is nowhere to send them.
suggestions.impact: Foundational for every future measurement claim.
suggestions.effort: Low once an endpoint exists; endpoint choice is the real work.
suggestions.risk: A frontend counter alone would look like analytics while measuring nothing — keep it inert until real ingestion exists.
options: A. Self-host a two-line ingestion endpoint (POST to a JSON-lines file) on any small VM; 30-day retention.
B. Privacy-first hosted analytics (e.g. Plausible-family tooling) with outbound-link events.
C. Stay inert; measure only via Associates reports.
suggestions.recommended: A for the pilot, revisit B at scale; add a privacy note either way
suggestions.prompt: Provision a POST-only ingestion endpoint that appends {event, path, ts} JSON lines (no cookies, no fingerprinting, no IP logging beyond the server's default), then set the site's analytics endpoint meta tag in the template so assets/js/site.js starts sending the five defined events, and document retention in the privacy section.

suggestions.title: Verify Search Console and schedule the first query review
suggestions.problem: The site is indexable but nobody is watching queries; Priority 4 says the next topic should come from measured queries.
suggestions.impact: High for topic selection; zero cost.
options: A. File-upload verification into the repo root, sitemap submitted, 30-day review scheduled.
B. DNS verification once a custom domain exists (pairs with S-12).
C. Defer until traffic exists (not recommended — nothing bootstraps itself).
suggestions.recommended: A now, B at domain switch
suggestions.prompt: Add the Search Console verification file to the repo root (placeholder committed now, swapped for the real token on owner request), submit /WinB/sitemap.xml, and write the review checkpoint into the desk page: 'first query review due <date +30d>'.

suggestions.title: Reader capture: switch the RSS block into an email list
suggestions.problem: The shop page's 'Friday shortlist' block points to the RSS feed; email is where affiliate audiences actually return.
suggestions.impact: High retention effect if the cadence is kept; meaningless if it isn't.
suggestions.effort: Provider choice + form embed; static site can host the form snippet fine.
suggestions.risk: A dead form is worse than none (the prior session's note stands). Any provider decision must include a privacy line and double opt-in.
options: A. Stay RSS-only until cadence is proven.
B. No-cookies, self-hosted double opt-in via the same VM as S-04's endpoint.
C. Third-party newsletter host on the chosen domain.
suggestions.recommended: A for 60 days, then B if publishing held cadence
suggestions.prompt: When the cadence log shows 8+ consecutive weekly posts, replace the RSS-only block with a double-opt-in form (provider TBD), add a privacy line, and gate the change behind scripts/validate_site.py so a form can never ship without a configured action URL.

suggestions.title: Grow the Air Fryer cluster to 12 guides, then stop and measure
suggestions.problem: Nine guides exist; the top-of-funnel needs enough surface for Google to categorize the site, but writing blind wastes effort.
suggestions.impact: Medium-high once Q-10 data exists; speculative before it.
suggestions.effort: One guide per week is sustainable; the scaffold script makes each ~40 minutes.
suggestions.risk: Volume without measurement is exactly the AI-slop failure mode the brief calls out.
options: A. Publish 3 more, pause for query data, continue with evidence.
B. 12 now (not recommended).
C. Freeze at 9 and deepen existing pages instead.
suggestions.prompt: Using scripts/scaffold_guide.py, draft three additional question-led guides in the air-fryer cluster (topics from the questions register, not keyword tools), each with a maker/listing evidence block, then hold further expansion until the first Search Console review (S-05).

suggestions.title: Seasonal shelf rotation: 'Holiday kitchen' edition for November-December
suggestions.problem: A publication signals seasons; a register doesn't. The gift angle also fits the two probes naturally.
suggestions.impact: Medium: better return visits and internal linking; supports 'looks published, not generated'.
suggestions.effort: Low: a shelf template plus 2-3 gift-framed intros (no new claims).
suggestions.risk: Seasonal copy must not imply price or stock promises (S-02 feeds it).
options: A. Season banner + re-framed copy on existing pages.
B. Full seasonal hub page with gift guide cluster.
C. Skip seasons until Q-10 data exists.
suggestions.recommended: A now; B if the season survives one review cycle
suggestions.prompt: Add a data/seasons.json consumed by the build (label, blurb, date range); render it as the front-page ribbon and shop banner so 'Season 1 · Holiday 2026' comes from data, not hardcoded HTML, and expires on schedule.

suggestions.title: Decide the authorship question (named human vs editorial desk)
suggestions.problem: Bylines currently say 'Counterwise Editorial Desk'. Search quality raters and readers both weigh named, qualified authors — but a name without genuine testing becomes a false claim.
suggestions.impact: High for trust and E-E-A-T; irreversible if faked (never fake).
suggestions.effort: Decision + bio page; testing (if chosen) is the real cost.
suggestions.risk: Manufacturing a persona would be exactly the dishonesty the compliance gate exists to stop.
options: A. Keep desk bylines; publish the method page; claim nothing beyond frameworks.
B. Recruit a real named editor with real testing photos and an 'How we test' protocol.
C. Hybrid: desk bylines now, named author per article once someone is contracted.
suggestions.recommended: A now, C when budget exists
suggestions.prompt: If a named editor is chosen: add site/data/team.json (name, role, real bio, contact), render author JSON-LD Person markup from it, and require every product claim they sign to reference a dated evidence row in the register. FTC endorsement guidance applies to any review claims: ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/ftcs-endorsement-guides-what-people-are-asking.

suggestions.title: Build the automation on the Creators API, not the deprecated PA-API
suggestions.problem: The original plan ('AI platform: automated product research, price analysis, article generation') assumed PA-API. Amazon's official notice deprecates PA-API 5 — new integrations receive 403 AccessDenied and are directed to the Creators API.
suggestions.impact: Strategic: prevents building the automation core on an API Amazon is turning off.
suggestions.effort: Read the Creators API docs; register via Associates account (owner-side credentials required — that is the gate).
suggestions.risk: None to the current site; the risk is building on the wrong foundation later.
options: A. Design the pipeline docs + data schemas around Creators API now (done in this build); implement after credentials exist.
B. Write PA-API code anyway (not recommended).
C. Manual-only forever.
suggestions.prompt: Read https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/creatorsapi/docs/en-us/introduction and implement a fetcher that writes dated snapshots into data/prices.json and data/ratings.json behind a credentials gate in the environment; no secrets in the repo, no fabricated fallback data.

suggestions.title: Keep the publishing workflow gated on four checks
suggestions.problem: Compliance items (disclosure, rel=sponsored, evidence links, blank-unverified) must never regress as volume grows.
suggestions.impact: High as a guardrail; invisible to readers.
suggestions.effort: One CI step — already wired in this build.
suggestions.risk: Gates that are easy to bypass defeat themselves; CI runs them on every push.
options: A. The four checks in scripts/validate_site.py run on every push and on every build-reproducibility diff (shipped).
B. Add a human sign-off step before merge (recommended when a second contributor joins).
suggestions.prompt: Extend validate_site.py with: (1) per-page freshness check for any dated evidence, (2) disclosure-text exactness check against the Operating Agreement sentence, (3) a rule that every 'listing shows' bullet must link to a captured observation.

suggestions.title: Move to a custom domain when the pilot is proven
suggestions.problem: A github.io path is fine for a pilot, thin for a shop brand; canonicals and feed URLs must all move together.
suggestions.impact: Medium: click-through and trust on the URL itself; also unlocks S-05-B and S-06-C.
suggestions.effort: Owner buys domain; repo holds CNAME; one build parameter changes every URL.
suggestions.risk: Forgetting a hard-refresh of Google's index post-migration — mitigated by keeping the old path live with canonicals.
options: A. Stay on github.io through the pilot.
B. Buy a short exact-brand domain before scaling content.
suggestions.recommended: A until S-05 review, then B
suggestions.prompt: Set the repo CNAME to <domain>, rebuild with --base https://<domain>, verify every canonical/sitemap/feed entry rewrites, and keep the github.io pages serving the same build for redirects.
